chunks: And it was said to Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: “Why did He make, in zina, four witnesses, and in killing, two witnesses?”
He said: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made mutʿah lawful for you, and He knew that it would be denied against you, so He made the four witnesses as a precaution for you.”
“And were it not for that, false accusations would have been brought against you, and rarely do four gather to testify to one matter.”

key_terms.احْتِيَاطاً: as a legal precaution and safeguard
key_terms.الزِّنَا: illicit sexual intercourse requiring a strict evidentiary standard
key_terms.الشُّهُودِ: witnesses whose testimony establishes a legal claim
key_terms.الْقَتْلِ: killing or murder in legal discussion
key_terms.شَهَادَةٍ: formal testimony in a judicial matter

ai.seo_question: Why are four witnesses required for zina in Islamic law while only two are required for murder?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal wisdom behind requiring four witnesses in cases of zina while only two are required in murder cases. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that this serves as a precaution connected to the lawfulness of mutʿah, so that people would not easily level accusations against believers.
